# Load Packages
```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(sf)
library(ggsflabel)
```
 
Code: 
 
## Create map of samples
 
### Load shapefiles
```{r}
can <- 
  read_sf("./shapefiles/lpr_000b21a_e/")
 
woodbisonpop <- 
  read_sf("./shapefiles/WoodBisonPop/")
```
 
### Set up map elements
#### Subset of Canadian Provinces
```{r}
can_subset <- 
  subset(can, PRENAME == "Alberta" | PRENAME == "Manitoba" | 
           PRENAME == "Northwest Territories" | PRENAME == "Saskatchewan" | 
           PRENAME == "British Columbia" | PRENAME == "Yukon")
```
 
 
### Extract General Latitude and Longitude for Herds
```{r, warning = FALSE}
herd_centroids <- 
  st_centroid(woodbisonpop) %>% 
  mutate(latlong = st_transform(geometry, 4326))
 
herd_centroids <-
  data.frame(herd = herd_centroids$POPULATION,
             status = as.character(herd_centroids$STATUS),
             latlong = as.character(herd_centroids$latlong)) %>% 
  mutate(latlong = gsub("c\\(", "", latlong),
         latlong = gsub("\\)", "", latlong)) %>% 
  separate(latlong, into = c("long", "lat"),
           sep = ", ")

herd_centroids <- st_centroid(woodbisonpop)

# 2. Add a 'label' column (since your ggplot calls for 'label')
# We will use the 'POPULATION' column as the label
herd_centroids <- herd_centroids %>%
  # Change labels
    mutate(POPULATION = case_when(
    # "Old Name from Shapefile" ~ "New Name for Map"
    POPULATION == "Aishihik Herd" ~ "AISH",
    POPULATION == "Chitek Lake Herd"    ~ "CL",
    POPULATION == "Delta"   ~ "WBNPPAD",
    POPULATION == "Elk Island National Park"   ~ "EINPW",
    POPULATION == "Etthithun Lake Herd"   ~ "ETH",
    POPULATION == "Garden River"   ~ "WBNPGR",
    POPULATION == "Hay-Zama Lakes Herd"   ~ "HZ",
    POPULATION == "Hay Camp"   ~ "WBNPHC",
    POPULATION == "Nahanni Population"   ~ "NAH",
    POPULATION == "Nordquist Herd"   ~ "NORD",
    POPULATION == "Nyarling"   ~ "WBNPNY",
    POPULATION == "Slave River Lowlands"   ~ "WBNPLB",
    POPULATION == "Wabesca"   ~ "WAB",
    POPULATION == "Ronald Lake"   ~ "RL",
    POPULATION == "Wentzel"   ~ "WENT",
    POPULATION == "Mack Bison CH-Range 2012_04"   ~ "MBS",
    # This last line catches anything you didn't rename and makes it Title Case
    TRUE ~ str_to_title(gsub("_", " ", POPULATION))
  ))

```
### Sample Sizes
```{r}
t1 <- analysis.gen[analysis.gen@other$YEAR.ASSIGN <=1999]
table(t1@pop)

t2 <- analysis.gen[analysis.gen@other$YEAR.ASSIGN %in% 2000:2015]
table(t2@pop)

t3 <- analysis.gen[analysis.gen@other$YEAR.ASSIGN >=2016]
table(t3@pop)

sample_counts <- data.frame(
    POPULATION = analysis.gen@pop,
    YEAR = analysis.gen@other$YEAR.ASSIGN
  ) %>%
  mutate(`Collection Year`= case_when(
    YEAR <= 1999 ~ "Pre-2000",
    YEAR >= 2000 & YEAR <= 2015 ~ "2000-2015",
    YEAR >= 2016 ~ "Post-2016"
  )) %>%
  # 3. Count samples per Herd per Era
  count(POPULATION, `Collection Year`, name = "n")


map_data <- herd_centroids %>%
  left_join(sample_counts, by = "POPULATION") %>% 
  filter(POPULATION != "WENT")
```


### Sample Map
```{r}

map_data <- herd_centroids %>%
  st_transform(st_crs(can_subset)) %>% # THIS IS THE KEY STEP
  left_join(sample_counts, by = "POPULATION") %>% 
  filter(POPULATION != "WENT")


facet_names <- c(
  "Pre-2000"   = "1986 - 1999",
  "2000-2015"  = "2000 - 2015",
  "Post-2016"  = "2016 - 2025"
)

# Now calculate the bbox from the correctly projected data
bbox <- sf::st_bbox(map_data)

# Run this BEFORE your ggplot code
map_data$`Collection Year` <- factor(map_data$`Collection Year`, 
                                     levels = c("Pre-2000", "2000-2015", "Post-2016"))
ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = can_subset, fill = "gray95", color = "white") +
  geom_sf(data = woodbisonpop, fill = "gray80", alpha = 0.2) +
  geom_sf(data = map_data, aes(size = n, color = `Collection Year`), alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_sf_text_repel(data = map_data, aes(label = POPULATION), 
                     size = 3, max.overlaps = Inf) +
  # Fixed the closing parenthesis here:
  facet_wrap(~`Collection Year`, labeller = as_labeller(facet_names)) + 
  scale_size_continuous(range = c(0.5, 4)) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom",
        axis.title.x = element_blank(), # Removes the 'X'
        axis.title.y = element_blank(), # Removes the 'Y'
        strip.text = element_text(face = "bold")) + # Optional: makes custom labels bold
  # Added a small buffer (expand = TRUE helps, but manual limits are safer)
  coord_sf(xlim = c(bbox["xmin"] - 1, bbox["xmax"] + 1), 
           ylim = c(bbox["ymin"] - 1, bbox["ymax"] + 1), 
           expand = TRUE)
```
